JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the L.R's of one deceased Sri.Krishnamurthy under Section 166 of M.V.Act,
1989 seeking (SCCH12) 3 MVC No.4793/2020 compensation of Rs.3,60,00,000/ ( Three Crore Sixty Lakhs only) in respect of death of one Sri.Krishnamurthy in Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 28.08.2020 at 8.30 pm one Krishnamjurthy had almost crossed TumkurBengaluru NH48 road, near Kaccha U turn Yedehalli bus stand, at that time, driver of one Lorry bearing No.KA36B1160 drove the same in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and zigzag manner and hit to Krishnamurthy and caused accident.
As a result he succumbed to the injuries and died on the spot.

The dead body was shifted to Nelamangala Govt. Hospital wherein,
post mortem was conducted and body was handed over to the petitioners.
Petitioners took the dead body to their village in a hired vehicle and performed last rite ceremony and obsequies by spending Rs.1,00,000/.

That petitioners have suffered mental shock and agony, pain and sufferings,
disappointment, anguish, frustration, loss of love etc due to the sudden death of the deceased in the accident.

That deceased was healthy prior to the accident and he was doing Pawn brokerage business and he was owning True Rise Finance and also he was doing SS trading which was all about selling paper and papers boards and he was also earning from tour and travels by hiring and plying vehicle he was into multiple businesses and earning Rs.10,00,000/ per annum.
The first petitioner is the wife of deceased, petitioners No.2 to 4 are minor children, petitioner No.5 and 6 are the parents of the deceased.

The Nelamangala Traffic police, Bangalore have registered a case in Cr.
(SCCH12) 4 MVC No.4793/2020 No.303/2020 for the offence P/u/S 279 and 304(A) of IPC u/s 187 of IMV Act.
The respondent is the insurer and respondent no.2 is the R.C. owner of Lorry both are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioners.
On all these grounds petitioners prayed to award compensation of Rs.3,60,00,000/ with costs and interest in the above case.
3. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel and filed written statement.

On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessors inoffice has framed following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 28.08.2020 at about 8.30 pm her husband Krishnamurthy had almost crossed Tumkur Bengaluru NH48 road, near Kaccha 'U' turn Yedehalli bus stand, at that time, a Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA36B1160 driven by its driver from Tumkur side at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner came in zigzag manner and dashed to her husband and caused accident, due to which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and he succumbed to the said injuries on the spot?
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, by whom and what is the quantum?

sentences.text: To prove his case 1st petitioner wife of the deceased by name Savitha is examined as P.W.1.

It shows that Nelamangala Police have registered Crime No.303/2020 against the driver of unknown lorry on 28.08.2020.

In the first information one Ashok, who is driver of the Ambulance on call from control room saying that some public informed the control room of Jazz Toll stating some unknown lorry hit one person and he should take ambulance to the accident spot, first informant went to the spot and found that one person aged 47 years hit by lorry and the victim died on the spot.

In the cross examination of P.W.1 it is suggested that the accident has not taken from the (SCCH12) 9 MVC No.4793/2020 alleged spot and she denied the same and she produced the C.D camera footage of the Jazz Toll in which, the opponent lorry passed on the date of accident.

The counsel for respondent no.1 contended that in those photographs, lorry number cannot be seen.
He further contended that there may be many such lorries and it cannot be said that accident took place from the same lorry.

Further there is no photo or footage the said lorry being causing accident to the victim as such, according to him the said photographs and CC TV footage of the Toll gate where lorry passed cannot be considered to say that the same lorry caused accident.
According to him, only to file false case the said lorry is implicated in the accident.
10. P.W.1 being not an eye witness.
She being wife of the victim who has not seen the accident, her evidence is not helpful regarding the point of negligence.

who filed case against the driver of the lorry.

In his cross examination he stated that, he had no problem to give police complaint on that day, but there were many people gathered after the accident, he gave lorry number to the police and went away from the spot.
He denied that there is no material to say that he gave lorry number to the police.

sentences.text: The suggestion that, his vehicle could not be seen in CCTV footage is denied.
The suggestion that he is giving false evidence is denied.

12. R.W.2, who is authorized representative of 1 st respondent company has stated that, since the case was registered against unknown vehicle, the lorry mentioned in the present case was never involved in the accident.
13. Now, it is necessary to notice on the basis of this evidence that, 2nd respondent is R.C owner of the lorry.
In his written statement he stated that accident occurred on account of negligence on part of the deceased who came across the road suddenly without observing the vehicular movements.
This goes to show that his lorry was on the spot and allegedly found that the deceased in the present case was suddenly entered the road without observing vehicular movements.

When owner of the lorry is attributing negligence on part of the deceased, certainly his vehicle must have been in the spot and driver of the said (SCCH12) 11 MVC No.4793/2020 vehicle must have been present at the spot.
In fact in the final report, one Basavaraju S/o Siddappa is shown as driver of the lorry and he has not appeared before the court to say that he was never present at the spot.
He has also not challenged the final report against him which attributed negligence on his part.

If the lorry in question KA36B1160 was never in the spot of accident but still the negligence is attributed to its driver in causing the death due to accident, certainly the driver must have questioned the final report.
But in his written statement itself owner stated that deceased was negligent.
He could have specifically stated that, he does not know anything about the accident as his lorry never hit the deceased.

The driver on whom final report is filed has not appeared before the court and stated that a false case is filed against him and he was not driving the lorry in rash and negligent manner on the alleged date of accident.
14. Further in the IMV report it is mentioned that no fresh damages due to impact, but in vehicle seizure panchanama it is mentioned that on right side bumper there is damage.
It is argued before this court that since no damages could be found on the vehicle the said vehicle was not involved in the accident.
It is necessary to notice that it is 12 wheel lorry hitting the pedestrian, certainly must not have caused any much damage to the vehicle instead it would cause severe injury to the human body.
Therefore, only because as per IMV report there was no fresh damage to the lorry, it cannot be said that lorry was not involved in the accident.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court (SCCH12) 12 MVC No.4793/2020 the contention of the respondents that the aforesaid lorry was never involved in the accident cannot be believed.

15. Further it is necessary to notice that in the written statement of 2nd respondent owner of the lorry stated that the deceased came across the road suddenly without observing vehicular movement/traffic on the road and deceased was negligent.
He has not appeared before this court to produce any documents in this regard, however in the pleadings he stated that, deceased was negligent.
In the sketch produced at Ex.P.3 it can be seen that deceased has almost reached near the 'U' turn and accident took place almost at the end of the road before the 'U' turn.

This goes to show that there was rough 'U'
turn which was made to cross the road and there was no zebra crossing as such nor there is signal.
That gives an indication that deceased without observing the vehicular movement was crossing the road at night time at 8.30 pm.
When deceased had not taken necessary caution while crossing the road certainly he was also negligent to some extent.
The statement of the owner as well as driver before the police was that the vehicle was loaded with hollow bricks loaded from industrial area and was going towards Bengaluru.
As such, it was loaded lorry which hit the pedestrian.

The deceased being pedestrian crossing the national highway where there was no signal or zebra crossing must have been cautious of the vehicular movements and his negligence is forthcoming from the rough sketch coupled with statement of driver and owner of (SCCH12) 13 MVC No.4793/2020 the lorry before the police and also written statement of the owner of the lorry i.e., respondent no.2.

Even respondent no.1 insurance company in its written statement at para 7 has stated as under;
It can be safely gathered that deceased Krishnamurthy S/o Gangahanumaiah was crossing the road where there was no zebra crossing due to negligent act the deceased Krishnamurthy S/o Gangahanumaiah accident took place.
No actionable negligence can be attributed against the driver of lorry bearing reg.No.KA36B 1160.

The deceased Krishnamurthy S/o Gangahanumaiah was solely responsible for the accident,
under these circumstances, the petition is liable to be dismissed.
16. This goes to show that even 1 st respondent has mentioned about negligence on part of the deceased in the accident.
As such, in the opinion of this court, contributory negligence has to be attributed to the deceased to some extent.

In view of the evidence available on record, this court is of the opinion that contributory negligence to the extent of 30% has to be attributed to the deceased and 70% negligence shall be attributed to the lorry driver.

On the basis of evidence on record,
petitioners have proved that driver of the lorry bearing no. KA36B1160 was negligent in driving the lorry and caused accident and on the basis of available evidence it is also proved that deceased was also negligent in crossing the road without (SCCH12) 14 MVC No.4793/2020 observing the vehicular movement near 'U' turn and his part of negligence is 30% in the accident.
Accordingly, I hold this issue in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE NO.2:
Since petitioners have proved negligence on part of the opponent lorry driver, they are entitled compensation at the hands of respondent no.1 and 2.
The 1 st respondent admitted the insurance policy, hence he is liable to indemnify the insured.
Respondents disputed the age of the deceased.
To prove his age petitioners produced his aadhaar card at Ex.P.16 which shows that he was born on 10.06.1973.
Accident took place on 28.08.2020.
At Ex.P.17 and 18 SSLC marks card and pan card of the deceased are also produced.
They all show the same date of birth of the deceased.
But to contradict the date of birth no other documents are produced by the respondents.
Hence in my view, it is proper to rely on that undisputed document in the absence any contrary evidence.
Hence, age of the deceased is considered as 47 years at the time of accident.
18. 1st and 2nd respondents disputed the occupation of the deceased.
In respect of occupation it is stated that, deceased was into multiple business.

In petition it is stated that, deceased was pawn G.Savitha vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90084341/

sentences.text: It is also stated that he was earning from tours and travels by hiring and plying vehicles and his earning was Rs.10,00,000/ per annum.
To prove the same his I.T returns, money lending licence, account statements in various banks (SCCH12) 15 MVC No.4793/2020 are produced at Ex.P.19 to 25.
On perusal of those documents, it can be seen that there is no document in respect of SS Trading regarding selling of papers and paper board and also earning from Tours and Travels.
However, there is money lending licence in the name of deceased which is valid from 03.12.2016 to 31.03.2021.
In 20192020 his gross total income was Rs.7,10,435/ and deductions were Rs.1,95,254/ and the net tax payable was Rs.16,157/.
Though these documents are disputed by the respondent side, there is no material to disbelieve that, deceased was not into business or his money lending licence was not valid.
In 20182019 his gross total income was Rs.8,13,764/.
In 20172018 his income was Rs.8,62,426/.
This goes to show that his income was varying from year to year and it was not stable.
He was not salaried person but was into private business as per the documents produced before the court.
Even his Firm was partnership firm as per Firm registration certificate produced at Ex.P.20.
It indicates that there were partners with him who would share the income and loss.
19. The petition shows that deceased was having 6 dependents and aged 47 years.
Therefore there are all chances that he would have made best efforts to earn higher amount of income to take care of his family.

Hence, in the opinion of this court, the average income of the deceased in 2020 when accident took place, on the basis of income tax returns produced by petitioners has to be considered as Rs.7,00,000/ per annum.

Accordingly, annual income of the deceased is (SCCH12) 16 MVC No.4793/2020 considered as Rs.7,00,000/ and monthly income Rs.7,00,000 / 12 = Rs.58,333/
per month.
20.
Petitioner No.1 is wife.
Petitioner no. 2 to 4 are minor children and petitioner no.5 and 6 are parents of the deceased.
All of them are legal heirs of the deceased Krishnamurthy.

Respondent no.1 and 2 disputed their dependency on deceased and that they are they legal heirs of the deceased, but as per the aadhaar card produced by the petitioners it can be seen that they are L.R's of the deceased and they will have to be considered as dependents of the deceased.
No separate income of petitioner no. 1, 5 and 6 is established to show that they are not dependents on the deceased.
Hence, in the opinion of this court, petitioner no.1 to 6 will have to be considered as dependents of the deceased.
21. In view of above reasons it is held that, the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 47 years and his income was Rs.58,333/ per month and petitioners are dependents on the deceased.
Hence, this issue is held Partly in the Affirmative.
22. ISSUE No.3:

In view of the reasons assigned above it is clear that, Sri. Krishnamurthy expired in the road traffic accident occurred on 28.08.2020 due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Lorry Reg.No.KA 36B1160 and therefore the L.R's of the deceased are entitled for compensation.
They are entitled for compensation on the following heads to the following extent.

sentences.text: Loss of dependency :
As per finding to Issue no.2, petitioners are held to be dependents on the deceased.
As per the Praney Sethi case future prospects of the deceased will have to be added to the monthly income.
In case of self employed 25% of the income has to be added to the monthly income to the age group of persons between 4050 years.
Age of the deceased in this case is 47 years.

Therefore, in the present case the monthly income of deceased is Rs.58,333/ + 14,583/ =72,916/
.
Further deceased being married having 6 dependents 1/4th of his income shall be deducted towards his personal expenses.

Hence, the loss of dependency is calculated as under;
Rs.54,687 X 12 months = Rs.6,56,244/
Rs.6,56,244/ X 13 multiplier to the age group of 4650 years = Rs. 85,31,172/
As such

, loss of dependency of the petitioners due to the death of their family member is Rs.85,31,172/
24.
Loss of love and affection: Petitioners being L.R's of the deceased have lost the love and affection of husband, father and son respectively due to the accidental death of their family member.
Therefore, for loss of love and affection compensation has to be granted.

There is no hard and fast rule in respect of measuring love and affection but, in the opinion of this court if amount of Rs.60,000/ is awarded for loss of love and affection, (SCCH12) 18 MVC No.4793/2020 the interest of justice would be met.
Accordingly, amount of Rs.60,000/ is awarded.
25. Loss of Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses:

As per the judgment in Praney Sethi's case, the quantum of compensation for Loss of Consortium is fixed @ Rs.40,000/ and loss of estate and funeral expenses is fixed @ Rs.15,000/ respectively and it is revisable at 10% every 3 years.
As such, under the head of loss of estate Rs.18,000/, for funeral expenses Rs.18,000/ and for loss of consortium Rs.48,000/ each to petitioner no.1 to 6 is awarded.

Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation as under:

(SCCH12) 19 MVC No.4793/2020 26. Liability:
Having found that petitioners are entitled to aforesaid amount of compensation now the fixation of liability to pay the said amount to the family of the deceased will have to be examined.
Respondent no.1 admitted the insurance policy with him in respect of the offending vehicle, hence he is liable to indemnify the insured and pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, I answer this Issue "Partly in the Affirmative".
27. ISSUE No.5:
Petitioners have sought for compensation of Rs.3,60,00,000/ in respect of death of Sri. Krishnamurhty in road traffic accident.
They have not claimed any rate of interest on the compensation amount.
But as per the settled law, the interest that could be awarded on the compensation is only 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till the payment.
Hence, in view of above reasons petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.62,40,621/ with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of payment.

1 st petitioner being wife of the deceased is entitled to 30%, petitioners no.2 to 4 are minor children of the deceased are entitled to 10% each and petitioner no.5 and 6 are the parents of deceased are entitled to 20% each of the total compensation.

In such apportionment 50% amount of petitioner no.1, 5 and 6 shall be ordered to be kept in F.D in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 50% shall be ordered to be released in their favour.
Petitioner 2, 3 and 4 being minors, entire compensation awarded to them shall be kept in F.D till the (SCCH12) 20 MVC No.4793/2020 date of their attaining majority.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.62,40,621/ with interest @ 6%
p.a. on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment from respondents No.1 and 2.
In view of valid insurance policy, respondent no.1 shall indemnify the insured and hereby directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this court within 3 months from the date of this order.
Out of the total compensation amount with cost and interest awarded to the petitioners, 1st petitioner being wife of the deceased is entitled to 30%, petitioners no.2 to 4 are minor children of the deceased are entitled to 10% each and petitioner no.5 and 6 are the parents of deceased are entitled to 20% each of the total compensation.

opennyai_summary.issue:
On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessors inoffice has framed following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 28.08.2020 at about 8.30 pm her husband Krishnamurthy had almost crossed Tumkur Bengaluru NH48 road, near Kaccha 'U' turn Yedehalli bus stand, at that time, a Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA36B1160 driven by its driver from Tumkur side at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner came in zigzag manner and dashed to her husband and caused accident, due to which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and he succumbed to the said injuries on the spot?
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, by whom and what is the quantum?
3 . What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When owner of the lorry is attributing negligence on part of the deceased, certainly his vehicle must have been in the spot and driver of the said (SCCH12) 11 MVC No.4793/2020 vehicle must have been present at the spot.
If the lorry in question KA36B1160 was never in the spot of accident but still the negligence is attributed to its driver in causing the death due to accident, certainly the driver must have questioned the final report.
But in his written statement itself owner stated that deceased was negligent.
Therefore, only because as per IMV report there was no fresh damage to the lorry, it cannot be said that lorry was not involved in the accident.
It was one way and G.Savitha vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90084341/
When deceased had not taken necessary caution while crossing the road certainly he was also negligent to some extent.
The statement of the owner as well as driver before the police was that the vehicle was loaded with hollow bricks loaded from industrial area and was going towards Bengaluru.
As such, it was loaded lorry which hit the pedestrian.
The deceased being pedestrian crossing the national highway where there was no signal or zebra crossing must have been cautious of the vehicular movements and his negligence is forthcoming from the rough sketch coupled with statement of driver and owner of (SCCH12) 13 MVC No.4793/2020 the lorry before the police and also written statement of the owner of the lorry i.e., respondent no.2.
No actionable negligence can be attributed against the driver of lorry bearing reg.No.KA36B 1160.
The deceased Krishnamurthy S/o Gangahanumaiah was solely responsible for the accident,
under these circumstances, the petition is liable to be dismissed.
As such, in the opinion of this court, contributory negligence has to be attributed to the deceased to some extent.
In view of the evidence available on record, this court is of the opinion that contributory negligence to the extent of 30% has to be attributed to the deceased and 70% negligence shall be attributed to the lorry driver.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, amount of Rs.60,000/ is awarded.
As per the judgment in Praney Sethi's case, the quantum of compensation for Loss of Consortium is fixed @ Rs.40,000/ and loss of estate and funeral expenses is fixed @ Rs.15,000/ respectively and it is revisable at 10% every 3 years.
As such, under the head of loss of estate Rs.18,000/, for funeral expenses Rs.18,000/ and for loss of consortium Rs.48,000/ each to petitioner no.1 to 6 is awarded.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation as under:
Sl.No. Particulars of Heads Amount in Rs.
Petitioners have sought for compensation of Rs.3,60,00,000/ in respect of death of Sri. Krishnamurhty in road traffic accident.
But as per the settled law, the interest that could be awarded on the compensation is only 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till the payment.
Hence, in view of above reasons petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.62,40,621/ with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of payment.
1 st petitioner being wife of the deceased is entitled to 30%, petitioners no.2 to 4 are minor children of the deceased are entitled to 10% each and petitioner no.5 and 6 are the parents of deceased are entitled to 20% each of the total compensation.
In such apportionment 50% amount of petitioner no.1, 5 and 6 shall be ordered to be kept in F.D in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 50% shall be ordered to be released in their favour.
Petitioner 2, 3 and 4 being minors, entire compensation awarded to them shall be kept in F.D till the (SCCH12) 20 MVC No.4793/2020 date of their attaining majority.
Hence, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.62,40,621/ with interest @ 6%
p.a. on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment from respondents No.1 and 2.
In view of valid insurance policy, respondent no.1 shall indemnify the insured and hereby directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this court within 3 months from the date of this order.
Out of the total compensation amount with cost and interest awarded to the petitioners, 1st petitioner being wife of the deceased is entitled to 30%, petitioners no.2 to 4 are minor children of the deceased are entitled to 10% each and petitioner no.5 and 6 are the parents of deceased are entitled to 20% each of the total compensation.
In such apportionment 50% amount of petitioner no.1, 5 and 6 shall be ordered to be kept in F.D in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 50% shall be ordered to be released in their favour.
Petitioner 2, 3 and 4 being minors, entire compensation awarded to them shall be kept in F.D till the date of their attaining majority.
